item.title: Enemalta cable works to close Sliema seafront bus lane for two months
item.description: Enemalta begins works on Wednesday to lay a new 4.5-kilometre 11kV cable from the Manoel Island distribution centre in Gżira to the Sliema Ferries area, with a further 2.7km of low-voltage cables to strengthen supply. During the roughly two-month project the bus lane running parallel to the seafront will be closed for excavation and cable-laying, and traffic heading out of Sliema will be reduced to a single lane. Enemalta said the existing cable had accumulated numerous joints over the years and had become increasingly vulnerable to faults, with demand having grown considerably.

item.title: Malta Tourism Authority carried out over 1,200 inspections in three localities
item.description: The Malta Tourism Authority carried out more than 1,200 inspections in San Pawl il-Baħar, Tas-Sliema and San Ġiljan, Tourism Minister Jo Etienne Abela told parliament in reply to a question by MP Graziella Galea. More than 500 of the inspections were carried out in Tas-Sliema, the highest number of the three localities.

item.title: Xjenza Malta steps up investment in cultural heritage research
item.description: Xjenza Malta has increased its investment in research into Maltas cultural heritage, which it says is part of the countrys identity and includes historic buildings, archaeological sites, underwater heritage, traditional skills and cultural practices. The agency said climate change and rising environmental pressures make the preservation of that heritage a significant challenge, underscoring the need for sustained research investment.

item.title: Three men jailed for six months over false travel documents
item.description: Mourtda Kasime Jaoud, 33, and Mohammed Hasan Mohammed Al Baaj, 24, both from Iraq, and Sakhr Al Gumaei, 36, from Yemen, pleaded guilty to possessing false travel documents after arriving in Malta on 2 November. Two held false Iraqi passports and the third carried Greek documents belonging to someone else. Magistrate Nadine Sant Lia sentenced each to six months imprisonment.

item.title: Nurses union asks government to exempt health workers from budget measures
item.description: The Malta Union of Midwives and Nurses has asked the government to exempt healthcare staff from the Budget 2027 measures that have increased their financial burden, and has requested an urgent meeting to discuss proposals. Around 1,200 third-country national nurses working in the public and private sectors have written to the union with their concerns. The measures announced last week include the removal of free childcare and free public transport for third-country nationals and higher driving-licence fees, which MUMN says threaten the health and elderly-care sectors.

item.title: 20 people died from excessive heat during July heatwave
item.description: Health Minister Ian Borg told parliament that 20 people died from hyperthermia during Julys heatwave, with 179 patients treated at Mater Dei. The figures were given in reply to a question by MP Darren Carabott on how many people were admitted with hyperthermia and how many died. Hyperthermia occurs when the body overheats and cannot cool itself effectively.

item.title: Ten domestic violence arrest warrants still outstanding
item.description: Ten arrest warrants linked to domestic violence cases remain unexecuted in Malta, Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield confirmed in parliament. Eight of the suspects are either abroad or untraceable, while two are receiving treatment at Mount Carmel Hospital. The information was tabled in reply to a question by MP Miriana Calleja Testaferrata de Noto.

item.title: Libya seeks extradition of Lilu King from Malta
item.description: The Libyan government has formally requested the extradition of Mohammed El Mushraty, known as Lilu King, from Malta. Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said the request was submitted in writing in September, and that all options are being considered before a final decision is taken.

Sources: MaltaToday

item.title: Survey finds majority of residents see no change in household finances from budget
item.description: A new independent survey by Marketing Advisory Services found 54.4% of Maltese residents said the budget measures made no notable difference to their household finances, while 34.2% said the measures improved their situation. Respondents prioritised cheaper prices for food and essential goods (42.3%), with the survey carried out as debate on Budget 2027 continues.

item.title: Mġarr ix-Xini valley rehabilitation works completed
item.description: Rehabilitation and clean-up works at Mġarr ix-Xini Valley, carried out over the summer to improve rainwater management, have been completed. The works covered about a kilometre from Triq Tal-Gruwa to the existing dam, removing vegetation from around 11,700 square metres and some 24,500 cubic metres of sediment. Gozo Minister Clint Camilleri said the intervention was intended to strengthen the valleys capacity to handle rainwater.

item.title: Tourists spending less despite record arrivals, Alex Borg says
item.description: Speaking at the Nationalist Partys Business Breakfast on Budget 2027, opposition leader Alex Borg said average tourist spending has fallen from 919 in 2015 to 771 in 2025 despite four million visitors in 2025. Citing Chamber of Commerce figures, he said rising visitor numbers are not translating into greater economic value while adding pressure on infrastructure, the environment and public services.

item.title: Freeport ordered to pay 35,000 to injured crane operator
item.description: Crane operator Roderick Bonnici was awarded 35,000 in damages after a 2020 workplace injury at the Birżebbuġa freeport facility. He was hurt when the cranes trolley suddenly lost control, jolting his cabin and injuring his leg and knee. Malta Freeport denied responsibility, but the court, presided over by Judge Henri Mizzi, found an abnormal deceleration had caused the incident.

item.title: Non-EU families put baby plans on hold as childcare centres fear closure
item.description: Some young non-EU families are postponing plans to have children because they now face paying for childcare in Malta. Centres catering mainly for these families fear that the budgets withdrawal of free childcare could force them to close. Only those who obtain long-term residency after five years and completion of the I Belong integration programme remain eligible for the free services.
